newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech flood toll rises, crops and industry hit.
newsitem.headline: Czech flood toll rises, crops and industry hit.

text.p: The death toll in a week of severe flooding in the Czech Republic rose to 43 on Tuesday as fears of the economic cost hit financial markets.
Severe disruption to road and rail links threatened some companies with closure and shares of flood-hit firms fell.
Agriculture Minister Josef Lux said damage to crops was estimated at about 1.25 billion crowns ($36 million) but that no extra imports would be needed.

Lux, who is also deputy premier, told a news conference total losses in the agricultural sector, including livestock, equipment and infrastructure and the crop damage, was an estimated 12 billion crowns.
"Although the damage is exceptional, I am not expecting any jumps in commodities prices nor shortfalls in domestic markets," Lux said. "We are not considering organising any imports."
The grain crop was the most severely affected, he said, adding the government would organise compensation for farmers.
The government has already approved the issue of five billion crowns in bonds and the release of a similar sum from privatisation proceeds for flood relief.
Police put the latest death toll from the floods, caused by days of torrential rain, at 43, CTK news agency said.
Share analysts said investor sentiment had taken another knock on fears that economic output may suffer.
"We're seeing some of the construction companies going up, but the companies that were hit by the flood are going down," said Jan Sykora of Prague brokers Wood and Company.
Czech steel mills and coal mines have been forced to cut output and may have to close due to the interruption of rail links, the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny said.
The paper said 900 railway carriages full of steel have piled up at the Nova Hut a.s. steel mill, in the northeastern region of Ostrava.
Shipments of steel and coal to neighbouring Poland and Slovakia remained interrupted, the paper said.
"If we don't get more empty carriages, we will be forced to stop the machinery, and that will cause a chain reaction in other firms," the newspaper quoted Karel Hybl of Nova Hut as saying.

Trucks seeking to cross from the Czech Republic into Slovakia are having to wait up to 50 hours in a queue about 10 km (six miles) long on the main highway between the two countries as several other border crossings are closed due to flooding, Czech Television reported.
